correctness.rationale: The center-membership case split is correct. With neither center chosen, every leaf subset is in general position. With only center \(u\), either no \(A\)-leaf is chosen and an arbitrary \(B\)-leaf subset is allowed, or exactly one \(A\)-leaf is chosen and no \(B\)-leaf is allowed; the symmetric statement holds for \(v\). With both centers, no leaf can be included. This gives \(\psi(D_{a,b};x)=(1+x)^{a+b}+x(1+x)^a+x(1+x)^b+(a+b+1)x^2\) and the stated maximal sets. A fresh independent geodesic enumeration for \((a,b)=(2,2),(2,4),(3,5)\) matched the polynomial and the maximal-set count \(a+b+4\); the package verifier independently checks all parameter pairs \(2\le a,b\le7\).

originality.rationale: Although the 2024 general-position-polynomial paper does not print a double-star or bistar formula, Anand et al. had already published a complete characterization of general-position sets in arbitrary connected graphs in terms of the components of the induced subgraph forming an in-transitive, distance-constant partition. Specializing that characterization to the diameter-three double star yields exactly the submitted center/leaf case split with only local inspection, and the 2024 polynomial paper supplies the counting-polynomial framework and inclusion-exclusion viewpoint. The submitted formula is therefore a routine special-family corollary of a stronger published structural characterization, so it is covered under the audit's implication rule.
